edgeDifference: Legacy selects in place on its loaded layer; core applies FlattenSession.setVariantOverride before begin(). The three-argument form maps to a prim-scoped key ("<prim>{<set>}"); the one-argument form, which legacy forces on every variant set, maps to one set-name override per set.

An idle call cancels nothing on either product; legacy records it as cancelRequested in its progress record, core does not. Next additionally reports and controls a running parse from the RenderStream progress callback; legacy loads synchronously without a JS callback and has no equivalent. Called from the callback it cancels the load (stage "cancelled").

Next authors every legacy attribute with the same values (URDF prim hierarchy, meshes, joints, collider purpose=guide, Newton scene settings and MuJoCo/Newton contact and mesh-collision attributes and APIs) and additionally authors mjc:timestep and mjc:contype/conaffinity.

knownDifference: Next product contract: failures report the core parser's located message ("Line N, column M: ..."); legacy reports its own parser error stack. Empty-string results for idle and successful loads match.

edgeDifference: Both rewrite the root layer's asset path; core packages the asset under the remapped name, while legacy keeps the original entry name and leaves the remapped reference dangling.
Next keeps mesh geometry arrays (points, faceVertexCounts, faceVertexIndices) in the stage export; legacy loses those the converter consumed. All other content matches.

knownDifference: Both describe the same prims in the same order, but core's physics JSON is its own contract: schema fallback properties and geometry arrays instead of legacy's specifier/flag/matrix fields and point/face counts.
